content.thinking:
This deployment recomputes the cumulative sum for every purchase index, making it O(n^2) - which explains the latency spikes as purchase histories grow, since it's an algorithmic complexity regression from a code change, not a config change, and its 17:37:00Z deploy time lines up exactly with when latency started climbing. I'm also noting the error rate doesn't seem to be affected the same way.

Instead, logs show ClientDisconnected errors likely from shoppers giving up as pages take too long to render, consistent with p50/p95/p99 latency spiking hard while error_rate stays relatively low with just minor upticks. This is clearly a bad deployment - shipped code with an O(n^2) algorithm causing severe latency and client timeouts, and I'm confident in that conclusion.

hypotheses.subject: spend_summary.average_spend_per_item
hypotheses.summary: The 17:37 deploy of io-shop changed average_spend_per_item to recompute a running sum over all prior purchases for every purchase in the list (an O(n^2) loop) instead of using the already-computed total, which is CPU/latency-heavy for shoppers with any real purchase history. This lines up exactly with the onset: p50 jumped from ~45ms to 277-460ms and p95/p99 from ~210/380ms to 2000-3800ms starting at the 17:37 bucket, the same minute the deploy landed, and the account-page ClientDisconnected errors (shoppers timing out/giving up) climb through the incident window.

supporting_evidence.claim: modified src/io_shop/spend_summary.py ... for index, _ in enumerate(account.purchases): spent_by_then = sum(earlier.price_cents for earlier in account.purchases[:index + 1])
ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection
